answer: Cap what one identity can earn and make presence itself cost time: every agent must periodically publish a liveness beacon chained to its own past work, with its reward rate capped. An honest agent on its own island of work simply keeps its beacon lit, but a Sybil farmer running a thousand fakes must keep a thousand separate beacons alive, each tied to distinct work — an echo of another agent's beacon is rejected outright, so mass forgery pays a thousandfold in continuous attention and compute, far more than capped rewards can return.
